newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle crew pack up for trip home.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle crew pack up for trip home.

text.p: The astronauts aboard the space shuttle Columbia packed up their science gear on Wednesday and prepared to return to earth after a trouble-free 16-day mission.
The crew of seven were shutting down the shuttle's bus-sized laboratory after a successful test of Columbia's landing systems, mission operations director Lee Briscoe told a news conference.
"The crew is busy turning the orbiter from a science platform back into a flying machine again," he said.
Although there was a chance of ground fog, weather conditions looked good for Columbia to touch down on schedule shortly after sunrise on Thursday, Briscoe said.
The winged spaceship had two landing opportunities at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre, the first at 6:47 a.m. EDT (1047 GMT) and the second at 8:22 a.m. EDT (1222 GMT), on orbit of the earth later.
Columbia's astronauts completed an $86 million research programme left unfinished in April when the shuttle had to return to earth after only four days because of a defective power generator.
It was the first time the U.S. space agency had sent a shuttle and its crew back to space to complete a mission.
Since blasting off on July 1, the crew conducted over 30 experiments in the shuttle's laboratory and ignited more than 200 controlled fires for combustion research.
"The science folks seemed very happy with the mission," Briscoe said.
